draft.title: Making bioethanol
card: Yeast breaks down glucose without oxygen to make ethanol and carbon dioxide. The glucose can come from crops such as sugarcane.
The mixture after fermentation is mostly water, with only a low percentage of ethanol. Too much ethanol makes the yeast stop working.
The mixture is heated so the ethanol boils off first, as it has a lower boiling point than water. The vapour is cooled and condensed to give a more concentrated ethanol.
The concentrated ethanol can then be used as a fuel, often blended with petrol.
draft.remember: Yeast ferments glucose to ethanol and carbon dioxide. Distillation then concentrates the ethanol for fuel.

a.q: What is the purpose of distillation in making bioethanol?
opts: To concentrate the ethanol by separating it from water
To turn glucose into ethanol and carbon dioxide
To supply the yeast with more glucose to use
To remove the carbon dioxide made by the yeast
a.why: Distillation uses the lower boiling point of ethanol to separate it from water and raise its concentration. Changing glucose into ethanol is fermentation, which happens earlier and is done by the yeast.
a.clue: Distillation separates substances by boiling point.

b.q: Lena heats a fermented mixture from her sugarcane batch in Bundaberg and collects the first vapour that boils off. Why is this vapour richer in ethanol?
opts: Ethanol has a lower boiling point than water
Ethanol has a higher boiling point than water
Yeast makes ethanol only at the surface
Carbon dioxide turns into ethanol when heated
b.why: Ethanol boils at a lower temperature than water, so it vaporises first and the early vapour has more ethanol. A higher boiling point would leave the ethanol behind in the flask.
b.clue: Which substance boils off first when heated?

a.best: To concentrate the ethanol by separating it from water

b.best: Ethanol has a lower boiling point than water
